(2024). MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv.
creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
description: MMMU is a college-level multimodal benchmark for expert-level understanding and reasoning. It contains 11.5K carefully selected questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks across six disciplines, 30 subjects, 183 subfields, and 30 image types, with interleaved text and images.
name: MMMU
rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators included over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the selected majors and coming from various disciplines and subjects.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper describes multi-stage quality control: lexical overlap and source URL similarity were used to identify potential duplicates, which were then reviewed by the authors; problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking; and authors categorized problems into difficulty levels, excluding approximately 10% classified as very easy.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students, including co-authors and subject specialists, collected multimodal college-level questions. Annotators were instructed that all questions must contain one or more images, be written in English, meet college-level difficulty, be unambiguous, and be categorized as multiple-choice or open-ended; they annotated question text, options, correct answer, image types, difficulty, and explanation if available. They were also instructed to follow copyright and licensing regulations and to avoid sources prohibiting copying or redistribution.
rai:dataBiases: The authors explicitly note that the manual curation process may carry biases. They also describe design decisions to mitigate bias and contamination, including selecting diverse sources, avoiding subjects where enough relevant multimodal problems could not be found, and advising annotators to select questions without immediately available answers to reduce data contamination concerns.
rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was curated in three stages: the authors selected 30 subjects from common university majors where visual inputs are commonly used, recruited over 50 university students including co-authors as annotators, and collected multimodal questions from online sources, textbooks, lecture materials, and quizzes, creating new questions based on expertise where necessary. The process yielded about 13K questions, which were then cleaned and filtered to form MMMU.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw source data consisted of multimodal college-level questions from free online resources, quizzes, textbooks, lecture materials, and other study materials, including images such as diagrams, charts, photographs, maps, tables, music sheets, chemical structures, and medical images.
rai:dataLimitations: The paper states that the manual curation process may carry biases and that the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. It also cautions that MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI because there is no direct mapping between benchmark performance and the '90th percentile of skilled adults,' and college exams are not the only tasks AGI should tackle.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The collected set of about 13K questions was filtered through quality control and difficulty curation; approximately 10% of problems labeled very easy were excluded, producing the final 11.5K-question benchmark split into dev, validation, and test sets.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: After collection, the data underwent cleaning by detecting potential duplicates using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, author review to remove duplications, format and typo checking for standardized formatting, and difficulty categorization into very easy, easy, medium, and hard. Approximately 10% of very easy problems were excluded from the benchmark.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The appendix includes a version change log with changes from V1 to V4, indicating versioned updates to results, URL fixes, author contribution statement additions, and model result updates.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper connects the benchmark to monitoring progress toward Expert AGI and notes societal importance because systems at this level could lead to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption. The benchmark is presented as a tool to monitor such progress and support development of next-generation multimodal foundation models.
rai:dataUseCases: MMMU is intended to evaluate large multimodal models on expert-level multimodal understanding and reasoning, monitor progress toward Expert AGI, benchmark perception, knowledge, and reasoning across professional domains, and stimulate development of next-generation multimodal foundation models.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The ethical considerations instruct annotators to avoid collecting questions that contain any private information.
